data.text: The council is underweighting three tail risks: (1) CN/Financials consensus is bearish at only 0.28 confidence with 0.67 dissent, yet the financials proxy gained 2.6% monthly—meaning a wrong bearish call here has the least data support and the most asymmetry if the market reopens and confirms the fiscal stress; (2) HK/Financials volatility at 26.56% is the highest of any sector in our data, making it the cell where a wrong directional call hurts most in absolute terms; (3) US 10Y yields at 5.277% with 15.23% volatility create a cross-market contagion channel that the council treats as a US-only problem, but which could amplify HK and CN financial stress simultaneously. The consensus on CN/Tech bearish is the most robust, but the council underweights the risk that PBOC easing (PSL cut to 1.5%) could produce a sharp relief rally that invalidates the bearish view.

data.plain_english: A report says China's housing slump has badly hurt the finances of its local governments. The council expects Hong Kong shares and Chinese technology companies are more likely to fall, since they were already sliding and this adds worry. In the US, sharply rising interest rates are the bigger story and are hurting banks. The council is split on US technology companies, which have been rising, and on Chinese banks, whose shares have held up so far. This is research, not advice to buy or sell.

risk.method: council view 35% (negative views only), volatility 25% (8-25%), 1-month drawdown 20% (0 to -6%), disagreement 10%, unverified claims 10%; portfolio adds up to 10 points for market concentration
